purpose: Read-mode editorial storyboard; original diagrams specified, not rendered assets.

modeContract.switchBehavior: Preserve shared lesson, practice answers, progress and preferences. Switching mode never resets or completes a lesson. Map Watch chapter cues to Read panel IDs; when no precise cue exists, switch at the same lesson and announce that position.
modeContract.fullText: Always expose Full lesson text as semantic HTML, including every original content paragraph, activity, knowledge check and referenced source. Never hide the only accessible equivalent behind animation.
modeContract.practice: Use the identical source activity and knowledgeCheck in both modes. Do not duplicate scoring or alter answer IDs.
modeContract.watchUnavailable: Keep Read accessible. Label Watch unavailable or preparing honestly; never display a fake playable asset.

deliveryNote: Compact derivative. Read original course JSON for verbatim content, activities, checks, source links and assessment keys. All diagrams are specified-not-rendered native HTML/CSS or accessible SVG. No production artwork is claimed. Canonical design artifact is read-storyboards.json.

panelDefaults.interaction: Explicit Next/Back and optional native details; no auto-advance. Keep callouts visible; full source text remains available.
panelDefaults.visualAssetType: original semantic diagram or native case card
panelDefaults.textEquivalent: Use panel copy plus mapped source paragraphs; use original numerical tables where specified.

courses.title: Adult Learning Theory: Design for the People Doing the Work

lessons.title: 1. Begin with the work, then test your assumptions

panels.title: Start with the required handoff
copy: Issue summary + next owner + next action.
Four of ten sampled handoffs lack owners.
Ask what prevents the required behavior.
panels.visualSpecification: Ten labeled sample tokens, four marked Missing owner; clearly fictional, with exact text count.

panels.title: Use adult-learning assumptions as questions
copy: Ask about purpose, self-direction, experience, readiness, problems and motivation.
Adults still vary in tool experience and needed guidance.
panels.visualSpecification: Six equal question cards, no fixed learner-type classification.
panels.callout: Andragogy is one theoretical perspective, not a universal explanation.

panels.title: Observe before prescribing
copy: Can the person find the owner list and submit a practice handoff?
Offer a guided example when needed.
Include access fixes in implementation.
panels.visualSpecification: Observe → ask → support sequence, with separate instruction and access routes.

panels.title: Try the decision, then check your reasoning
copy: Choose a response and explain the evidence behind it.
Read the option-specific feedback, then try the knowledge check.
panels.visualSpecification: One original case card above a semantic radio-choice group. Feedback appears directly under the chosen option; knowledge check follows as a separate step in the same panel. No decorative character art needed.
panels.callout: Practice remains available in both Read and Watch. Selected-response success does not establish production mastery.

lessons.title: 3. Offer relevant choices and the support to succeed

panels.title: Make the task relevant
copy: Practice the decision that creates a usable handoff.
Motivation differs across people and situations.
panels.visualSpecification: Owner-and-next-action decision card, with a purpose statement rather than decorative workplace photography.

panels.title: Offer equivalent ways to engage
copy: Choose password-reset or order-status practice.
Keep the same required fields and criterion.
Offer text, optional demonstration and checklist.
panels.visualSpecification: Two equal case choices linked to a common requirement; persistent Read/Watch controls remain separate.
panels.callout: Options support access and task needs, not fixed visual/auditory/kinesthetic learner types. Required privacy and safety controls remain.

panels.title: Vary the case, preserve the standard
copy: Choose novice and experienced-colleague examples.

Check performance rather than confidence alone.

lessons.title: 5. Plan transfer and measure what changed

panels.title: Separate three kinds of evidence
copy: Learning: decision-check results.
Behavior: handoff completeness.
Conditions: access, time and expectations.
panels.visualSpecification: Three clearly labeled evidence cards; completion counts shown separately as implementation evidence.
panels.callout: Improvement after training does not establish that training caused it; form redesign may also matter.

panels.title: Support the first real attempts
copy: Provide a one-screen checklist.
Managers review early attempts privately.
Route access problems to the system owner.
panels.visualSpecification: Point-of-work support loop with checklist, supervisor feedback and authorized access route.

panels.title: Make a transfer plan
copy: One practice task.
One point-of-work support.
One responsible person.
One observable behavior to review.
